study type: Multilevel analysis of pooled Demographic and Health Survey data
cohort: 95,348 mother-baby pairs in 22 sub-Saharan African countries
finding: Several factors were associated with increased likelihood of prelacteal feeding, including caesarean section delivery, lower maternal education, first or fourth or above birth rank, short preceding birth interval, lower antenatal care visits, home delivery, multiple birth, male infant, and average or small infant size at birth.
mod_finding: Caesarean section delivery was associated with a 2.25 times higher odds of prelacteal feeding compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery.
birth_weight: Average or small size at birth associated with prelacteal feeding
